title: Register clearing run
statement: Let $P$ be a register program with $m$ registers, $d$ deciders, and state set $\Lambda$, let $\mathcal O$ be an oracle, let $r$ be a register, and let $c_R,c_E,\mathit{next}\in\Lambda$. Suppose the transition function in state $c_R$ agrees on every input symbol and tuple of scanned register symbols with the specified action that begins the clearing run on register $r$, and in state $c_E$ agrees on every such input and tuple with the specified clearing action leading to $\mathit{next}$. Suppose also that neither $c_R$ nor $c_E$ is an oracle-call state. For every configuration $c$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$, there is a time $T$ such that execution from the configuration obtained from $c$ by setting register $r$ to the tape encoding of the binary digits of $n$, with its head at $0$ and state $c_R$, reaches the configuration obtained from $c$ by setting that register to the tape encoding of the binary digits of $0$, with its head at $0$ and state $\mathit{next}$. At each time $t<T$, the configuration has some state $s$ that is not an oracle-call state, and the head position $q$ of register $r$ satisfies $-1\le q\le$ the length of the binary digit list of $n$.
